memo.verdict: Neutral; park. Corbion (CRBN-NL) at €22.40 (2026-09-25) is a self-help margin recovery in a medium-quality fermentation business with a cyclical pricing trough in its most profitable segment laid on top; not a growth case, not a demand inflection, not an oversold compounder. The modal return is about 11% a year over eighteen months and over three years against the 20% bar, a D, because the multiple (13.3x consensus EPS 24 months forward) has already recovered from about 10x to the stock's own five-year median while consensus EPS fell 12% to 17%, and because the two prices that set 2027 earnings, wild fish oil and the US dollar, are not Corbion's to set. Two dated triggers to progress: the Q3 2026 trading update in late October 2026 showing a Health & Nutrition segment margin at or above 29% with positive pricing, or a binding agreement to sell the 50% TotalEnergies Corbion PLA joint venture at or above €100 million. One price trigger: about €20, at which the modal path clears the bar over eighteen months (about €18 for the three-year case). Conviction medium on the analysis, low on the direction of the two external prices; Triaging depth. The park rule's gates do not park the case (management C; business quality C; predictability read as transmission B; trackability B); it is parked on the return. Nothing invalidates it today; the Invalidate levels are a FY2026 Health & Nutrition margin below 27%, a FY2026 Functional Ingredients & Solutions margin below 10.5%, no joint-venture agreement by 31 July 2027 or a price below the €69.2 million book value, EUR/USD above 1.30, and a fish-oil price below US$3,300 a ton sustained through a contract round.
case: - The change is internal, real, dated and about half done. Emulsifiers was sold to Kingswood for US$362 million (about €255 million; net proceeds €251.8 million; a €138 million net book profit), closing 2 April 2024; frozen dough was divested in 2021; the Peoria plant was mothballed; about 200 roles were removed for €35 million of recurring fixed-cost savings at a €9.4 million charge; €15 million of stranded costs were fully compensated over 2024 to 2025; a second cost programme started in Q2 2026; the 50% TotalEnergies Corbion PLA joint venture has been held for sale since late 2025 with advisers engaged (€1.6 million of fees in H1 2026), a binding agreement expected within twelve months of 31 July 2026 and TotalEnergies a willing co-seller; sugar and dextrose (34% of raw-material spend; sugar alone 28%) are hedged for 100% of 2026 and nearly 100% of 2027 and early 2028 at a five-year-low price. Capital expenditure was cut from €231 million in 2022 to €68 million in 2025. The top team below the chief executive and the board were substantially renewed in eighteen months. The screen's false-positive red flags are all absent.

- What is missing from the pattern: no chief-executive change (KQ F), and the only guidance move in the period was a cut (KQ D); the sell-side calls BRIGHT 2030 "evolution, not revolution", and ING calls the 18% 2028 target "not overly ambitious" against its own 19%.

- The external forces net to a mild headwind, and the two that set 2027 earnings are outside Corbion's control. Of seven forces: three headwinds (competition D, tightening on three fronts; macro D, the dollar at 71% to 80% of revenue unhedged at translation, €2.3 million to €2.4 million of EBITDA per 1% move, the 2025 fall costing €12 million to €13 million of EBITDA and €44.4 million of sales; supply logistics, freight and sulfuric acid at €15 million to €20 million gross in 2026), two tailwinds (regulation B, the EU Listeria rules from July 2026 and the EU packaging regulation from August 2026, against the emissions-trading free-allowance phase-out and the non-GMO wall on AlgaPrime in Western human nutrition; the company's own volume cycle, which has turned), two mixed (demand C, structurally growing at mid-single digits, natural preservation 4% to 5% a year, the omega-3 addressable market €3.3 billion to €4.8 billion by 2030, the Q2 rebound the end of destocking, not an inflection; disruption C, long-dated). The wild-catch fish-oil price is disputed in direction: the bear reading a trough of US$2,950 a ton below a US$3,300 AlgaPrime breakeven, ING expecting Corbion forced to US$3,500, 30% of AlgaPrime volume on spot and the US$4,000 to US$5,000 contracts expiring in late 2026; the bull reading El Niño supply constraints in Peru, a reduced second-season quota moving the price 21% in a week, and management saying prices are structurally rising and will substantially increase from Q3 2026. The Peruvian anchoveta quota is the leading indicator every research report names.
counter_case: The Q2 2026 print is the inflection the sell-side missed, and the record is wrong to park. Destocking is over and volumes are growing double-digit across every platform but pharma (group volume and mix plus 10.7%; Health & Nutrition plus 16.9%; Biomaterials double-digit in every region). Functional Ingredients & Solutions recovered 250 basis points of margin in one quarter, to 11.5% from 9.0%, with sugar and dextrose locked to early 2028 at a five-year low and a second cost programme starting, so the 12% segment target is in reach without heroics. Fish oil is tight on El Niño; a reduced Peruvian second-season quota moved the price 21% in a week; the 2023 aquaculture contracts rolling off are to be replaced by higher-priced ones from Q3 2026, taking Health & Nutrition back to a 30% margin by year-end, which is exactly what management promised on 31 July 2026 ("substantially increase"). The €15 million to €20 million freight and sulfuric acid headwind is a one-year cost that reverses, and it is already in guidance. The joint venture sells within twelve months for about €100 million against €69.2 million of book value, TotalEnergies being a willing co-seller and the EU packaging regulation from August 2026 supporting PLA demand, and the proceeds fund a buyback as in 2024. The 2028 target of 18% is "not overly ambitious" (ING models 19%). So FY2027 EPS lands at ING's €1.75 or Oddo's €1.84 rather than the €1.51 consensus median; estimate momentum turns from D to B; and a business at the cheapest multiple in its dashboard set, with a 3% dividend yield, a 7% free-cash-flow yield on the €270 million target, a cash-generating balance sheet at 2.0x and a €100 million disposal in hand, re-rates to 15x to 16x on 2028 earnings of €1.90 to €2.10, giving €28 to €34 in eighteen months, a 25% to 50% return, with the three Buy targets at €25 to €26 as the sell-side's own floor for that view. On the Foundations, the returns are depressed by a completed capital-expenditure cycle whose depreciation is fixed while its output (the 125 kt Rayong plant; the Orindiúva algae expansion) is only now filling, so return on capital employed rises mechanically as utilisation passes 80% and the joint venture leaves the balance sheet; the moats (50% share; the strain library; GMP lock-in) are A-grade and cash conversion above 100% proves it. On the setup, the case fits 'OSHQC CfC Clearing' better than the record allows: the concern (fish-oil-linked pricing plus one freight shock) is transient by construction, contracts reset and freight lanes reopen, the quality gate is passed on the moats even if not on the returns, and "oversold" should be read against the ten-year median of 17.5x rather than the two-year median of 11.5x, on which reading the shares are a B fit and a re-rating to 15x to 17x is the modal outcome. On the case, it is simpler than the record makes it: three of the four external prices are hedged or nearly so (sugar locked to early 2028; freight in the guidance; fish oil tight), leaving the dollar; the concerns are many but small; the downside is bounded by the yield and the balance sheet. If a reader argues that a business with all its sugar hedged, no bioplastics and a 7% free-cash-flow yield deserves the top of its own five-year range, the anchor is the five-year 75th percentile of 16.93x, at which the eighteen-month value is €32.0 plus €0.67, a 46% return, 29% a year.

The record's concessions: the volume turn is real and printed; the cost base is locked; the freight cost is in the guidance and is transient; the three latest broker revisions (September 2026) are Buys; the direction of capital employed is down (€1,236.3 million to €1,145.9 million in 2025, with a €69.2 million disposal to come); the moats are real; the concern is largely transient; the ten-year band exists; the cash yield and the balance sheet are as stated. If the Q3 2026 update prints a Health & Nutrition margin near 30% with positive pricing, the eighteen-month arithmetic becomes a B at 14x and an A at 15.5x, and the record would move the odds on the cleared branch from one in three to about one in two and the 'Modal return' rating from D to C or B.
triggers: - The Q3 2026 trading update, late October 2026: a Health & Nutrition margin at or above 29% with positive pricing progresses the case (the record would move the cleared-branch odds to about one in two and the 'Modal return' from D to C or B); a segment margin below 28% is the Alarm; a FY2026 segment margin below 27% invalidates. This is the observation every research report and the record name as the one that changes the view.

- The joint-venture sale: a binding agreement at or above €100 million progresses the case; no binding agreement by 31 March 2027 is the Alarm; none by 31 July 2027, or a price below the €69.2 million book value, invalidates. Watch process announcements, the €59.5 million related-party loan balance and the joint venture's own margin (5.3% in Q1 2026).
- Price: about €20 clears the bar on the modal path over eighteen months; about €18 over three years.

- Functional Ingredients & Solutions: any quarter below a 10.5% margin, or negative segment volume, is the Alarm (negative volume makes the margin guidance mathematically unachievable); FY2026 below 10.5% invalidates.

- The US dollar: EUR/USD above 1.20 sustained is the Alarm; above 1.30 invalidates (13.6% of normalised EPS at 1.30; 44.5% at 1.60). The modal path assumes EUR/USD within about 5% of the 2025 average of 1.13.
- Wild fish oil: below US$3,500 a ton is the Alarm; below US$3,300 sustained through a contract round invalidates. Watch the Peruvian anchoveta quota.
